On October 16, 2026, Katarzyna Nurowska of the University of Warsaw presented balloon and ground measurements of radiation fog in a valley near Strzyżów, Poland. The fog core held about 0.2 to 0.4 grams of liquid water per cubic metre and up to about 300 droplets per cubic centimetre, with droplets of 8 to 10 micrometres near the ground that got smaller with height.

The same group is testing a way to measure fog without flying anything into it: one radiation station sits above the fog layer and one below, and the difference in sunlight and infrared reaching each reveals how much water the fog holds overhead. Existing radiation networks could then track fog continuously.

Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar was born on October 19, 1910, in Lahore. On the voyage from India to Cambridge in 1930 he calculated that a white dwarf cannot be heavier than about 1.44 Suns, now the Chandrasekhar limit; he shared the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics, and NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory is named after him.

In December 2025 Paul Kalas of UC Berkeley and colleagues reported in Science that Hubble had caught a second planetesimal collision around Fomalhaut, a new dust cloud called cs2 that appeared in 2023 images. The bodies that smashed together were about 30 km across, and two such crashes seen in about 20 years is far more often than the one per 100,000 years earlier theory expected.

Fomalhaut b, announced in 2008 as one of the first exoplanets photographed directly, is now thought to have been an expanding dust cloud from an earlier collision, not a planet. Kalas warns that such clouds can mimic a planet's reflected light for years, a trap for future planet-hunting telescopes.

A July 2026 simulation study of radiation fog in Italy's Po Valley found that more aerosol particles mean more, smaller droplets that settle more slowly, keeping fog around up to 54 minutes longer.
Radiation fog forms when clear skies let the ground radiate its heat to space. The chilled air next to the ground cools to its dew point and, being dense, drains downhill to pool in valleys.

In July 2026, smoke from Canadian wildfires turned New England skies yellow. Smoke particles absorb blue and violet light and let yellow, orange and red through, and the thicker the smoke, the stronger the tint.
Smoke and dust particles are much larger than air molecules and scatter light by Mie scattering. The effect is strongest at sunrise and sunset, when sunlight crosses the most air.

facts.text: NOAA's forecast issued October 7 expects quiet conditions tonight, then minor to moderate storms on October 9 when a CME launched on October 6 arrives.

The January 19, 2026 storm reached G4 after one of the fastest CMEs in decades, but its magnetic field (Bz) turned strongly northward. That limited the energy reaching Earth, and auroras stayed mostly at high latitudes.

Even on the October 9 storm night, NOAA's top forecast of Kp 5.67 is below the level usually needed here. A camera on a long exposure, aimed north from a dark spot, will pick up faint red glow that the eye misses.
